data.title: NRx Pharma rises as FDA completes initial review of ketamine product
data.description:
Shares of NRx Pharmaceuticals (NRXP) rose on Friday after the company announced that the FDA didn't identify any major deficiencies as part of an initial review of its marketing application for its preservative-free ketamine product.

The regulator didn’t identify any drug-related review matters during the first-cycle review of its ANDA, the company said, adding it is not required to submit any new clinical or drug-related findings to prove the product’s safety and efficacy.

However, the FDA questioned whether the luer lock tip of the medication vial would properly operate when attached to a syringe, which the regulator classified as a major deficiency. 

However, following a clarification meeting with the FDA on Aug. 6, NRx Pharma (NRXP) cites a substantially de-risked path to approval, noting that three ANDA-approved products currently on the market use the luer-lock medication vial.

“We are encouraged by FDA’s commitment at the meeting to review this remaining information in the shortest-possible review cycle and remain focused on advancing our ANDA toward approval and commercialization,” CEO Jonathan Javitt remarked.

data.title: Lyft's results leave analysts split over AV threat, pricing
data.description:
Lyft (LYFT) shares reached their highest level in 6 months and pierced the 200-day moving average on another quarter of better-than-expected quarterly results and record-setting ride/rider metrics.

“We achieved an all-time high of over 30 million active riders, proving that rideshare is embedded in people’s everyday lives,” noted Lyft CEO David Risher.

The company achieved double-digit gross bookings, active riders, and total revenue, underscoring the company’s successful efforts to expand into new markets and engage new partners.

For the current quarter, Lyft (LYFT) expects gross bookings to increase another 15% to 19% to a range that straddles the consensus estimate of $5.58B estimates.

RBC Capital’s Brad Erickson: We like the favorable mix shift the company is leaning into with partner rides now 30% of total, other higher-value modes, airport rides, etc. We continue to detect very low confidence in Lyft and negativity around ride-hailing in general, given Waymo is poised to enter double digits in more cities in the U.S. With that said, the ride-hail market continues to demonstrate secular growth with Lyft rationally keeping pace, which we’d view as not appreciated in the shares. Outperform, $20 price target (was $18).

BofA Securities’ Justin Post: The AV debate, not results, will be the top driver of the stock price. We have preferred Uber as we think Uber’s balance sheet and scale make the company better positioned to integrate [autonomous vehicles]. However, we acknowledge that Lyft could make a very interesting AV partner for an Uber competitor. Underperform, $18 price target (was $17).

Wells Fargo’s Ken Gawrelski: Print and guide both modestly ahead of expectations but would prefer a mix of greater volumes and less price. We are concerned about higher headline prices and a steady diet of consumer incentives to stimulate demand. Equal Weight, $19 price target (was $18).

Oppenheimer’s Chad Larkin: Despite a strong quarter, the Q3 outlook is largely in line with the street and therefore not enough to impact investor sentiment. However, with results no longer missing street estimates, shares will likely move higher as investors exit short positions, particularly with shares trading 6x 2027 EBITDA. Outperform, $20 price target.

data.title: Volkswagen controlling shareholders urge faster overhaul as Chinese rivals intensify pressure
data.description:
Volkswagen's (VWAGY) controlling shareholders have urged the German automaker to speed up its restructuring plans, warning that delays could undermine its ability to compete with Chinese carmakers, CNBC reported on Friday.

"The decisions that Volkswagen makes now will determine its future," Hans Dieter Pötsch, chairman of Porsche SE's management board, said, describing Volkswagen (VWAGY) as being at a 'historic crossroads." He said the company should focus on measures needed to strengthen its long-term competitiveness.

Volkswagen (VWAGY) has said it is considering cutting up to 100,000 jobs as it seeks to address falling profitability, rising tariff costs, and mounting competition from Chinese automakers.

Johannes Lattwein, Porsche SE's board member responsible for finance and IT, said it was “imperative” for Volkswagen (VWAGY) to reduce excess capacity, lower costs, and strengthen decision-making and execution. He added that Porsche SE supported Volkswagen's (VWAGY) management and that "every option must be considered" to improve the group's competitive position.

A Volkswagen (VWAGY) spokesperson said Porsche SE's comments were consistent with the automaker's restructuring plans and reinforced the urgency of carrying them out.

Chief Executive Oliver Blume has said Volkswagen (VWAGY) has already begun implementing its turnaround strategy, while Chief Financial Officer Arno Antlitz said the company's priority is to improve productivity, lower costs, and increase factory utilization rather than pursue job cuts or plant closures for their own sake.

data.title: Chesapeake outlines $1.2B Florida Energy Pathway project targeting 2030 in-service, while lifting 2026 capex to $550M-$600M
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Chesapeake Utilities Corporation (CPK) Q2 2026

Management view

  • "Our growth trajectory has continued through the second quarter as we reported a 5% increase in adjusted net income, driving an 8% increase in adjusted earnings per share through the first six months of this year," said (President, CEO & Chairman Jeffrey Householder), adding, "In the second quarter, we generated an incremental $10 million of margin" and "invested $140 million of capital in the second quarter" with "total year-to-date investment" of "$262 million."
  • "We just announced" the Florida Energy Pathway Project (FEP) and described it as "a 97-mile intrastate natural gas transmission infrastructure project" and "the largest single project in our company's history," representing "total investment of approximately $1.2 billion," said (President, CEO & Chairman Householder). He said Peninsula Pipeline "will fund and own at least 51%" and that FEP is "expected to be in service in 2030" and "anchored by multiple investment-grade shippers who've committed to nearly 250,000 dekatherms per day of capacity."
  • "We're increasing our full year 2026 capital guidance by $100 million, resulting in an updated range of $550 million to $600 million," said (President, CEO & Chairman Householder), citing "initial spending for FEP" and "increases in regulated distribution and infrastructure investments."
  • "We now expect to exceed $2.2 billion of capital investment from 2024 through 2028" and said the company will provide on the February 2027 full-year 2026 earnings call "2027 through 2031 capital expenditure guidance" and "2027 through 2031 earnings growth rate," according to (President, CEO & Chairman Householder).
  • "Adjusted gross margin was approximately $150 million" and "adjusted net income was approximately $25 million," while "adjusted earnings per share were $1.05," said (Senior VP & CFO Jeffrey S. Sylvester). He said the EPS result "is reflective of the shares we've issued throughout the last year as we return to our target capital structure."

Outlook

  • "We are updating" the five-year capital range and "now expect to exceed $2.2 billion of capital investment from 2024 through 2028," said (President, CEO & Chairman Householder), and added, "we now expect to provide" in February 2027 "2027 through 2031" capital guidance and "earnings growth rate."
  • "We remain committed" and are "reaffirming our 2028 earnings per share guidance of $7.75 to $8," said (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester).
  • Compared with last quarter’s messaging about revisiting the capital range by February 2027, management tied the timing and scope more directly to FEP, with (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) saying progress "particularly with the announcement of FEP, will necessitate a more fulsome update of our long-term performance expectations."

Financial results

  • "Ongoing and recently completed natural gas transmission expansion projects contributed $0.15 of adjusted earnings per share" and "margin from our infrastructure program investments accounted for an additional $0.10 per share," said (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester). He also cited "$0.06 of incremental adjusted EPS" from distribution demand and "$0.06 of improved propane and Aspire performance."
  • Offsets included "$0.04" tied to "consumption, quarterly timing differences and other items" and "$0.04 from decreased CNG, RNG and LNG services," plus expense items including "$0.11 of increased depreciation, amortization and property tax" and "financing activity... reduced adjusted EPS by $0.05," according to (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester).
  • Balance sheet and liquidity actions included: "we have just completed an amendment of our revolving credit agreement, bringing the total borrowing capacity under the revolver to $650 million, an increase of $200 million," said (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester), and noted "70% of our total debt capacity of $798 million available" as of June 30.

Q&A

  • Constantine Lednev, Wells Fargo: asked about FEP regulatory/permitting, shipper interest, upsizing, and how it fits the February update; (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester) responded, "we do expect there's growth in that potential project" and "we expect to have" the partnership "aligned here in the quarter," while (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said it is "jurisdictional to the Florida Public Service Commission" and that the route will be "largely in the public right of way" with permitting expected "to go relatively smoothly for a project of this size."
  • Lednev, Wells Fargo: asked why use a partner and about funding structures; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said partnering helps "maintain a reasonable balance on the risk" and reflects managing earnings while building "capital up to about $600 million on our side of the project" before revenue begins in 2030.
  • Michael Brown, Barclays: asked whether there is common ground for a Florida City Gas (FCG) rate-case settlement; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said, "I don't know that we will get to a settlement... and we're certainly prepared to fully litigate it if we need to."
  • Brown, Barclays: asked about EPS guidance for 2027 and beyond 2028; (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester) said, "We're not signaling it here" but will provide "more clarity" on "the five-year growth rate and the capital" in February 2027.
  • Tate Sullivan, Maxim: asked about FEP timing and whether it is the first intrastate partnership; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said capacity shortfalls were recognized "back in the mid-'90s" and that it will be the first: "Yes, that's exactly right. It is."
  • Sullivan, Maxim: asked about potential WRU expansion approvals; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said, "I'd like to think that it's a given. I never assume that," adding that LNG facilities are "the least expensive way and most efficient way" to meet Delmarva demand.
  • Christopher Ellinghaus, Siebert: asked about Virginia feasibility and Canaveral; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said Accomack work is "beginning the feasibility analysis" and Canaveral requires securing property, adding, "we think there's a real opportunity... and we're going to continue to be pretty aggressive." Ellinghaus also asked about broader customer-growth slowing; Householder replied, "Yes. I mean we are seeing some slowdown" but "nothing alarming to us at this point."
  • Paul Fremont, Ladenburg: asked how management will present a longer-term growth rate with a "lumpy" FEP profile; (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) said, "I'm not sure we've settled on exactly how to tell that story yet," but investors should expect "at least some visibility across the five years."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical around regulatory outcomes and long-range earnings visibility, highlighted by questions on settlement prospects and longer-term EPS framing; (Barclays’ Brown) asked directly if there is "a common ground for a settlement" and pressed for EPS guidance beyond 2028.
  • Management’s tone in prepared remarks was positive and expansion-focused, with (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) calling FEP "a valuable long-term regulated growth opportunity" and (Senior VP & CFO Sylvester) saying, "I remain highly confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results." In Q&A, responses were more cautious on uncertainty, including (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) saying, "I don't know that we will get to a settlement" and "I'm not sure we've settled on exactly how to tell that story yet."
  • Versus last quarter’s transition-focused tone (retiring CFO and incoming CFO), this call’s tone centered more on execution and scale, particularly the "largest single project" announcement and the expanded capital plan.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Strategic focus shifted from evaluating South Florida capacity options in Q1 to announcing FEP in Q2, with (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) describing FEP as a committed, shipper-anchored project expected in service in 2030.
  • Capital messaging changed from Q1’s $450 million to $500 million 2026 capex range to Q2’s "updated range of $550 million to $600 million," driven by FEP and broader regulated investment.
  • CFO leadership transitioned fully: Q1 introduced Jeff Sylvester as "incoming" CFO and featured outgoing CFO Beth Cooper; Q2 reflected Sylvester delivering the CFO financial update.
  • Analyst questioning broadened from Q1’s equity-financing mechanics and project exploration to Q2’s emphasis on FEP permitting/partnership structure, the FCG rate case litigation risk, and how long-term growth will be communicated.

Risks and concerns

  • Regulatory risk in Florida was explicit, with (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) saying on the FCG rate case, "we're certainly prepared to fully litigate it if we need to."
  • Execution and timing risk around large capital projects was embedded in the need to manage earnings before FEP revenues, as (President, CEO & Chairman Householder) referenced building capital "to about $600 million on our side of the project" before service in 2030.
  • Demand and mix risks included "some slowdown" in customer growth (Householder) and "decreased CNG, RNG and LNG services" (Sylvester), alongside expense pressure items such as higher depreciation, insurance, and customer-related costs (Sylvester).

Final takeaway

Management presented Q2 as a step-up in scale and long-duration visibility, anchored by the newly announced $1.2 billion Florida Energy Pathway Project targeted for 2030 in-service, alongside a $100 million increase to 2026 capex guidance and a plan to refresh multi-year capital and growth-rate disclosures in February 2027. The call also underscored near-term uncertainty around the Florida City Gas rate case, with management indicating it may proceed without settlement, while reiterating 2028 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.75 to $8 and highlighting ongoing financing capacity expansion through a larger revolving credit facility.

data.title: Tech stocks take off as earnings results, powered up by AI deals, propel market higher
data.description:
A wide range of technology and AI-exposed stocks were climbing on Friday, supported by a deep list of strong earnings results reported during the week.

For example, indie Semiconductor (INDI) shares had surged more than 15% by noon trading following its second quarter results. Meanwhile, Corsair Gaming (CRSR) rocketed more than 30% after reporting its second quarter results and outlook.

Five9 (FIVN) jumped more than 15% after it forecasted AI-related revenue to increase by at least 60% year over year for 2026.

"AI revenue grew 78% year-on-year, and we are increasing our full-year AI growth outlook from more than 40% to at least 60% year-on-year," said Five9 CEO Amit Mathradas.

He explained in detail how AI has strengthened, not disrupted, Five9's software platform.

"Contact centers are going through a major transformation," Mathradas said during Thursday's earnings call. "Service is no longer viewed only as a cost center to contain. Increasingly, enterprises see customer experience as a lever for loyalty, retention and growth. They want to resolve more issues, respond faster, personalize more interactions and create better outcomes for customers at scale. AI is enabling that shift by automating routine work and improving the economics of service. In many customer conversations, the ROI is becoming clearer, better service, more capacity, faster response times and stronger customer outcomes."

Other enterprise software firms were also demonstrating how AI was benefiting their projections. Appian (APPN) shares surged 14% on Friday following its second quarter results and outlook on Thursday.

"Some companies are clearly going to benefit from AI," said Appian CEO Matt Calkins in an interview with Seeking Alpha. "We are absolutely a beneficiary of the day. It is a clear benefit for us. There is no confusion or delay. There is only acceleration and growth."

"We are a complement to AI," he added. "When you want AI to do important work, you need a deterministic layer. We provide it. We provide a suite of functionality that allows you to use AI safely and effectively. We are a boost to AI. I think what everybody can agree on is that AI needs a software counterpart."

Semiconductor and software firms were both taking part in Friday's rally, as evidenced by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) and the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) increasing by 2% and 3%, respectively.

data.title: Onto Innovation stock jumps 13% on $1.1B backlog, upbeat outlook, AI demand
data.description:
Onto Innovation (ONTO) stock jumped over ~13% to ~$306 on Friday after the company reported a strong set of Q2 earnings and gave an optimistic outlook for the coming quarters. The rally pushed the stock's gain for the week to nearly 23%.

Moreover, the stock has been one of the best performers in the semiconductor sector this year, gaining 96.61% year to date, compared with the S&P 500 (SP500)'s 12.63% return in the same period.

The biggest reason behind Onto Innovation's price surge was a record second quarter with a revenue of $343.1M, up 35% from a year ago, while non-GAAP earnings rose to $1.93 per share from $1.25 last year.

The company said revenue, profit margins, and earnings all came in above the high end of its guidance.

Growth was driven by strong demand for AI-related semiconductor technologies. Revenue from advanced nodes jumped 50% from the previous quarter, while advanced packaging and specialty devices also reached record levels, supported by demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), 2.5D packaging, and silicon photonics.

Investors were also encouraged by the company's record backlog of more than $1.1B, providing better visibility into future sales.

Looking ahead, Onto Innovation expects Q3 revenue of $380M-$400M and non-GAAP EPS of $2.18-$2.38. Management also raised its second-half revenue growth outlook to 25% or more, saying strong AI demand could continue well into 2027.

The company also enjoys strong support from analysts. Wall Street has a 'Strong Buy' rating, while Seeking Alpha and the Quant system rate the stock 'Buy,' reflecting confidence in the company's growth outlook.

data.title: U.S. equities advanced after a weaker than forecasted payrolls report
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages traded towards the topside on Friday after July's nonfarm payrolls surprised to the downside, showing an unexpected contraction in employment.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.1%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +1%. 

From a sector-by-sector perspective, seven of the 11 S&P segments pushed up in the green and were led by consumer discretionary, while financials struggled the most. 

U.S. nonfarm payrolls declined by 23K in July, missing the +88K consensus and erasing the 20K increase in June, according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on Friday. What's more, June's growth was scaled back by more than half from the initial print of 57K. Unemployment slipped to 4.1% from 4.2% in June, lower than the 4.2% consensus. 

“The weaker-than-expected jobs report likely doesn't change much for the Federal Reserve, as Chair Warsh is allowing the data to guide policy and the data as of now likely warrants keeping rates at current levels,” Brent Wilsey of Wilsey Asset Management stated. 

Treasury yields moved lower across the curve. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) dropped 4 basis points to 4.20%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) slipped by 2 basis points to 4.65%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) was down 2 basis points to 5.20%. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Airbnb (ABNB) advanced by 15.1%, while shares of The Trade Desk (TTD) fell 20.2%.

data.title: Interface signals FY2026 net sales of $1.455B-$1.485B with ~40.6% adjusted gross margin
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Interface, Inc. (TILE) Q2 2026

Management view

  • “Interface delivered another strong quarter, exceeding our expectations, achieving 4% year-over-year currency-neutral net sales growth… Growth was broad-based across regions, product categories and primary market segments,” said (President, CEO & Director Laurel Hurd). “Profitability also improved significantly this quarter, driven in part by the IEEPA tariff refunds we recognized. More importantly, continued operational execution improvements also contributed to margin expansion.”

  • “Noravant timber… is gaining momentum in the market… we’re seeing encouraging specification activity from leading design firms,” said (CEO Hurd). “We believe noravant represents a meaningful opportunity to further expand in Healthcare and other segments over time.”

  • “We’re continuing to invest in automation and robotics to improve efficiency and expand margins… investments are exceeding expectations,” said (CEO Hurd), pointing to robotics in Europe and Australia, “new packaging automation in Australia,” and “robotics in Germany to enhance efficiency in our rubber business.”

  • “Second quarter net sales were $395.7 million, up 5.4% as reported and 3.8% on a currency-neutral basis,” said (VP & CFO Bruce Hausman). “Second quarter adjusted gross profit margin was 45%, up 524 basis points… The remaining 393 basis points were driven by a $15.6 million benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds and represented approximately $0.19 of earnings per diluted share.”

Outlook

  • “With a healthy backlog, strong order momentum and the margin performance we achieved in the first half, we are raising our full year guidance,” said (CFO Hausman). “We are not assuming any additional refunds going forward.”

  • “For the third quarter of fiscal 2026, net sales of $370 million to $380 million; adjusted gross profit margin of approximately 40.8% of net sales; adjusted SG&A expenses of approximately $100 million; adjusted interest and other expenses of approximately $4 million,” said (CFO Hausman), adding “an adjusted effective income tax rate of approximately 27.5%” and “fully diluted weighted average share count of approximately 58.2 million shares.”

  • “For the full fiscal year of 2026… we anticipate net sales of $1.455 billion to $1.485 billion; adjusted gross profit margin of approximately 40.6% of net sales; adjusted SG&A expenses of approximately $395 million… adjusted interest and other expenses of approximately $15 million… an adjusted effective income tax rate of approximately 26% and capital expenditures of approximately $60 million,” said (CFO Hausman).

Financial results

  • “Second quarter adjusted operating income was $74.9 million… Second quarter adjusted net income was $51.5 million… Second quarter adjusted EBITDA was $87.7 million… and second quarter adjusted earnings per diluted share was $0.88,” said (CFO Hausman).

  • “We generated $38.4 million of cash from operating activities and capital expenditures were $12.2 million,” said (CFO Hausman). “We also repurchased $8.8 million of Interface common stock and paid our quarterly dividend.”

Q&A

  • Brian Biros, Thompson Research Group: “Can you talk about the margins for Q3 and Q4… the puts and takes?” VP Hausman: “It’s just the timing of the flow-through… we feel really good about gross margins going forward.”

  • Brian Biros, Thompson Research Group: asked whether the guidance raise was “just the Q2 beat.” CEO Hurd: “Nothing has really changed… We came in a little bit better in Q2.”

  • David S. MacGregor, Longbow Research: asked to “bridge… the 131 basis points.” VP Hausman: “The automation and robotics… are a large piece… these are durable and structural changes.”

  • Alexander Paris, Barrington Research: asked about tariff refunds and whether it was “one and done.” VP Hausman: “It was a onetime refund… we’re still subject to tariffs, and we’re still paying tariffs every single day going forward. And that’s baked into our guide.”

  • Reuben Garner, The Benchmark Company: asked about SG&A and freight inflation. VP Hausman: “The freight… lands on the cost of goods sold line… the increase… is mostly due to variable selling commissions… variable comp… and… foreign currency.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts were slightly positive, with repeated emphasis on sustainability of gross margins, tariff mechanics, and operating expense discipline, including “a lot of focus around gross margins” (David S. MacGregor, Longbow Research) and scrutiny of the “one and done” nature of the refund (Alexander Paris, Barrington Research).

  • Management tone was positive and confident in prepared remarks and Q&A, using language such as “we feel really good” (VP Hausman) and “we’re committed to continuing margin expansion” (CEO Hurd), while also limiting forward assumptions: “We are not assuming any additional refunds going forward” (VP Hausman).

  • Versus last quarter, Q2 discussion shifted from potential refunds being “a really dynamic situation” (VP Hausman, Q1) to confirming receipt and financial impact: “a $15.6 million benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds” (VP Hausman, Q2).

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q2 emphasized margin expansion tied to a specific one-time item, while Q1 framed tariff refunds as uncertain: “There’s nothing assumed in our guide around the tariff refund” (VP Hausman, Q1) versus “we also recorded a $15.6 million tariff refund in the second quarter” (VP Hausman, Q2).

  • Segment growth mix shifted, with Q1 highlighting “Corporate office… billings were up 16%” (CEO Hurd, Q1) and Q2 calling out “Healthcare had a standout quarter with global billings up 19%” (CEO Hurd, Q2).

  • Backlog language stayed constructive but strengthened in magnitude: “Backlog… up 18% year-to-date” (CEO Hurd, Q1) versus “Backlog… up 22% year-to-date… giving us confidence to raise our full year guidance” (CEO Hurd, Q2).

Risks and concerns

  • “We’re seeing low single-digit inflation cost increases in our raw materials,” said (VP & CFO Hausman), adding that proactive pricing and inventory timing affects near-term margin cadence.

  • “We’re still subject to tariffs, and we’re still paying tariffs every single day going forward,” said (CFO Hausman), while noting the refund was “a onetime refund.”

Final takeaway

Interface’s management described Q2 as broad-based growth with sharply higher profitability, while tying a meaningful portion of margin upside to a one-time $15.6 million IEEPA tariff refund and highlighting continued structural gains from automation, mix, and pricing execution. The company raised full-year guidance and outlined Q3 and FY2026 targets, while repeatedly stressing it is “not assuming any additional refunds going forward” and that ongoing tariff and raw-material inflation pressures remain embedded in its outlook.

data.title: AEye reaffirms $30M-$35M 2026 cash use as it ramps output for 2H
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: AEye, Inc. (LIDR) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "I'm excited to report that our overall momentum continued in the second quarter... having grown to our highest level of engagement yet" (CEO & Chairman Matthew Fisch). "I'm pleased to announce that we have been selected as the preferred lidar vendor for a groundbreaking sports analytics provider."
  • "Q2 revenue grew approximately 9x year-over-year and roughly 100% quarter-over-quarter, marking our fourth consecutive quarter of growth" (CEO & Chairman Fisch). "Proof-of-concept programs from revenue-generating customers grew to 25 from 21 since our last earnings call and both engagements and quote activity increased approximately 25% and 40% quarter-over-quarter, respectively."
  • "Defense continues to be our most active vertical with engagements doubling quarter-over-quarter" (CEO & Chairman Fisch). "Our lead defense customer placed its third consecutive paid order this quarter" and "our partnership with Fintech... continues to actively promote and ship Apollo to its customers."
  • "Apollo was recently validated on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor" (CEO & Chairman Fisch). "OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers building on the NVIDIA DRIVE platform can source Apollo as a prequalified sensor, reducing integration risk and shortening the path from system design to deployment."
  • "Second quarter revenue was $202,000" (CFO, Treasurer & Chief Business Development Officer Conor Tierney). "Two components drove the quarter" including "$30,000 of contract development revenue from customer-funded engineering work."

Outlook

  • "We're reaffirming our 2026 full year cash use outlook of $30 million to $35 million" (CFO Tierney). "We expect second half consumption to run higher than the first half as we start to ramp the manufacturing build."
  • "We have begun ramping our output to match our forecast of increased customer demand in the second half of the year" (CEO & Chairman Fisch). In Q&A, he added: "We're just focused maniacally on quarter-on-quarter growth... The last 4 quarters. we've doubled quarter-on-quarter consistently. We aim to continue down that path here in the back half of the year."
  • "We announced one commercial win. But we think we're on the one yard line here with a few other customer announcements" (CFO Tierney). "We expect to probably getting some news out here in the next few months or so."

Financial Results

  • "Second quarter revenue was $202,000" (CFO Tierney), including product revenue where "repeat orders from our lead defense customer continued to grow in size quarter-over-quarter" and "we started shipping units to Alive3D," plus "$30,000 of contract development revenue."
  • "GAAP operating expenses were $10.6 million versus $8.9 million in the first quarter" (CFO Tierney). "Non-GAAP operating expenses... were $8.2 million compared to $7.4 million."
  • "We reported a GAAP net loss of $10 million or $0.22 per share" and "on a non-GAAP basis, our net loss was $7.6 million or $0.17 per share" (CFO Tierney).
  • "Second quarter cash consumption was $7.5 million compared to $9.2 million in the first quarter" and "we ended the quarter with cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of approximately $71.5 million" (CFO Tierney).

Q&A

  • Richard Shannon, Craig-Hallum: asked to "quantify" the 2H output ramp and which end markets drive it; CEO & Chairman Fisch said, "we're fully loaded with 25 different customer programs" and "we expect that to continue through the back half of the year," while CFO Tierney added, "we think we're on the one yard line here with a few other customer announcements."
  • Richard Shannon, Craig-Hallum: asked about contract development revenue end market and future contribution; CFO Tierney said, "this customer was in the aerospace and defense sector" and "we're going to see contract development revenues become a more meaningful number on our P&L," while CEO & Chairman Fisch said, "the customer is putting skin in the game... and that comes along with product sales as well."
  • Richard Shannon, Craig-Hallum: asked about auto RFIs/RFQs and timing; CEO & Chairman Fisch said, "we had a new evaluation start" and "we've had an RFQ come in," but "automotive programs take a lot longer time to process."
  • Charles Fratt, Alliance Global Partners: asked what attracts and retains customers; CEO & Chairman Fisch said, "we'll call it the 1 kilometer sensing range headline" and "we give that flexibility through the software defined" approach, adding, "there is some fierce competition" and "that's why we won that project."
  • Charles Fratt, Alliance Global Partners: asked about defense interest and broadening use cases; CEO & Chairman Fisch said Q2 saw "a very large influx of counter UAS" and described it as "counter drone detection," while CFO Tierney added, "we may initially engage with the customer about one particular use case" and then "that may lead to opportunities elsewhere."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts slightly positive: Richard Shannon said, "Congrats on a really nice quarter" and sought more detail on the 2H ramp; questions focused on production scaling, contract development revenue durability, and defense demand broadening.
  • Management positive and confident: CEO & Chairman Fisch said, "As a company, we're hitting our stride" and later, "we're really excited about what's around the corner in the back half of the year," while CFO Tierney said, "conversion is no longer theoretical."
  • Current vs. previous quarter tone: Q1 opened with "steady execution, no surprises" (CEO & Chairman Fisch), while Q2 emphasized new proof points such as "selected as the preferred lidar vendor" for Alive3D and being "validated on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor" (CEO & Chairman Fisch).

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Pipeline and conversion language sharpened: Q1 highlighted "more commercial engagement than at any point in our history" and customers rising "from 15 to 21" (CEO & Chairman Fisch), while Q2 reported "proof-of-concept programs... grew to 25 from 21" and stated "repeat business is now a pattern rather than an exception" (CFO Tierney).
  • New revenue stream and vertical: Q2 added "$30,000 of contract development revenue" (CFO Tierney) and announced sports analytics with Alive3D; Q1 discussion centered on expanding engagements and partner ecosystem without citing contract development revenue.
  • Production posture shifted: Q2 said, "We have begun ramping our output" (CEO & Chairman Fisch); Q1 framed manufacturing as a strength and highlighted a capital runway narrative but did not describe a production ramp.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Automotive programs take a lot longer time to process" (CEO & Chairman Fisch), and OEM evaluations were described as a "long process."
  • "We expect second half consumption to run higher than the first half" as manufacturing builds ramp (CFO Tierney).
  • Cost variability was flagged through higher operating expenses tied to "nonrecurring engineering, tooling and test costs" and "noncash stock-based compensation" (CFO Tierney).
  • Competitive intensity was acknowledged in sports analytics: "there is some fierce competition" (CEO & Chairman Fisch).

Final Takeaway

Management described Q2 as an inflection in commercial validation, pointing to Alive3D selecting Apollo in sports analytics, Apollo being validated on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor, and defense remaining the most active vertical with repeat orders and expanding use cases. The company reiterated its $30 million to $35 million 2026 cash use outlook while preparing for higher second-half cash consumption tied to manufacturing ramp, and emphasized that repeat business, contract development revenue, and multiple near-term customer announcements are intended to support continued quarter-on-quarter revenue growth.

data.title: Voya says Toms Capital materials contain inaccurate, misleading statements
data.description:
Voya Financial (VOYA) said Toms Capital materials contain "inaccurate and misleading" statements and reproduce media reports that contain false information about the company.

"These materials describe a fictitious shareholder meeting in a manner and format that is liable to confuse and deceive our investors," Voya said in a  statement on Friday.

The response comes after Toms, which has a 4.5% stake in Voya (VOYA), on Thursday announced it filed proxy materials to provide holders with the opportunity to consider and vote on a non-binding resolution. The non-binding resolution allows shareholders to convey unequivocally that they “no longer continue to have confidence" in the board and management of Voya.

Voya (VOYA)  advised its holders that there is no upcoming meeting and there are no matters for holders to vote on for which proxies could be solicited. Voya also highlighted that it held its annual meeting in May.

Toms in June repeated a call for Voya (VOYA) to explore its options, including a sale of the company, and engage with interested buyers. Reports in April indicated that Toms had taken a stake in Voya (VOYA) and was pushing for the company to put itself up for sale or offload its underperforming health insurer arm.
